correctness.rationale: The source gives the exact meridian parametrization \(\rho=\sec(t-h_{\lambda,N}(t))\), the finite expansion of \(h_{\lambda,N}\), and the nontrivial first coefficient \(\phi_1(t)=(1+4\cos(2t))/(48\pi)\). Differentiating at \(\lambda_0\) gives the exact profile \(-\sqrt3(1+4\cos(2t))/(24\pi)\). Its maximum and minimum are \(\sqrt3/(8\pi)\) and \(-5\sqrt3/(24\pi)\). A uniform \(O_N(\delta^2)\) remainder on the compact angular domain justifies passing to global maxima and minima, including the sign reversal for \(\delta<0\). Rotation adds no new radial values. Hence the oscillation coefficient is exactly \(\sqrt3/(3\pi)\). The proof does not use finite experiments to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: The source's main geometric separation mechanism is that sectional data can be accurate to high order while the body remains linearly non-spherical, but the stated theorem quantifies non-sphericity only by an unspecified constant. The exact coefficient \(\sqrt3/(3\pi)\) calibrates that mechanism, identifies the complete first-order radial mode, and shows that every truncation order has the same intrinsic linear departure from the ball. This is a natural structural invariant of the newly constructed bifurcating family and a reusable benchmark for any future convergence or stability analysis.
